value.rationale: The first vertex of a fixed small offspring degree is a natural age extremum in an evolving tree. Fixed-degree classes have logarithmically different first-occurrence scales, even though their global populations are linear, and after degree-specific scaling all classes have independent Poisson frontiers. The result identifies the earliest-at-most-K degree with probability tending to one, a sharp structural prediction unavailable from global fixed-degree means or per-vertex Gaussian laws.
